summary: On a Mac the menu bar and the window's own menus show the Cmd keys for Refresh, Open and Quick Look. `key_table(mac, cx)` in src/actions.rs binds four keys ahead of the shared table when `mac` is true: Cmd+R -> Refresh (FINDER), F5 -> Refresh (FINDER), Cmd+O -> OpenSelected (FILES) and Cmd+Y -> QuickLook (FILES); and it binds Cmd+O -> OpenSelected (FILES) once more in the `if mac` block at the end. The macOS menu bar shows an action's first binding (gpui-pre-macos 0.3.10 `create_menu_item`: `bindings_for_action(..).find_or_first(..)` against Zed's own contexts, which fffinder's never match), so View › Refresh, File › Open and File › Quick Look get Cmd+R, Cmd+O and Cmd+Y as what they show and as their key equivalents, where they had F5, Return and Space. The kit's menus show the last binding whose keys run the action from where the menu looks, so the Mac's item menu shows Cmd+O for Open too; it showed Return, because the folder tree's Return is bound after the files' Cmd+O. Linux and Windows keep Enter there. The F5 binding was added in review: with Cmd+R on Refresh, the only menu bar item left with F5 is Window › Copy to Other Pane, and a key the window doesn't take is the menu bar's to try. Bound in the FINDER context, F5 outside the file views refreshes on a Mac whatever the menu bar does; in the file views the table's two F5 bindings have the deeper context and still win. `key_table(false, cx)` is the same bindings in the same order as before. docs/manual.md: Open joins the paragraph at the top of "Keyboard shortcuts" about the commands that show Finder's key on macOS and the other file managers' elsewhere.
changelog: On macOS, the menu bar shows Cmd+R for View › Refresh, Cmd+O for File › Open, and Cmd+Y for File › Quick Look, where it showed F5, Return, and Space. The item menu shows Cmd+O for Open there too, instead of Return. In the file views Return, Cmd+Down, Space, and F5 do what they did, and nothing changes on Linux or Windows.
behaviour_changes: macOS, from reading GPUI's macOS menu code and from binding the Mac's table on Linux (Ctrl stands in for Cmd), not run on a Mac: the menu bar shows Cmd+R for View › Refresh (was F5), Cmd+O for File › Open (was Return) and Cmd+Y for File › Quick Look (was Space). Those are the items' key equivalents now.

macOS, same basis: the item menu shows Cmd+O beside Open (was Return, which a Mac draws as ⏎). Quick Look in the item, Trash and Actions menus, Refresh in the background menu, and the "Show as Text" tooltip in Quick Look showed Cmd+Y and Cmd+R already and still do.

macOS, same basis: F5 is bound to Refresh for the whole window. In the file views nothing changes: it refreshes in a window with one pane and copies to the other pane in split view. Outside them (search field, filter field, sidebar, folder tree, a name being edited) it refreshes, in split view too, and copies nothing. If macOS offers a plain F5 to the menu bar, which I believe but could not run, that is what it did before through View › Refresh, and without the binding it would now have reached Window › Copy to Other Pane (a warning with one pane, a copy in split view). If macOS doesn't offer it, F5 did nothing outside the file views before and refreshes there now.

macOS, by reading only: Cmd+O and Cmd+Y, as menu key equivalents, should now reach Open and Quick Look where the window has no binding for them: in the search field, the filter field, the Nushell field and the sidebar, and while a name is being edited in place. Before, they did nothing there. In the folder tree Cmd+O does what Return does there (gives the keyboard to the files). It is what a click on the menu item always did. While a dialog has the keyboard (tried: Go to Folder, Settings, Search Syntax, New File) the items are unavailable and nothing happens, as before.

macOS: Return and Space are no longer menu key equivalents. They were never live as such (a space typed in the search field doesn't open Quick Look today), and their bindings are untouched, file views only, so nothing changes.

A key bound more than once acts once. On a Mac Cmd+O is bound three times in the file views, Cmd+Y twice, Cmd+R twice in the window, and F5 reaches Refresh by two bindings in a one-pane window's files.

Linux and Windows: no change. `key_table(false)` binds the same keys in the same order, pinned by a unit test, and my picture of the item menu is pixel-identical to the implementer's from before the change apart from the free-space figure in the status bar. F5 there is still a key of the file views only.

docs/manual.md: the paragraph at the top of "Keyboard shortcuts" lists Open with Back, Forward, Enclosing Folder and Move to Trash, with Cmd+O on macOS and Enter (the Return key) on Linux and Windows.
left_out: Nothing was run on macOS or Windows. No test can assert what the macOS menu bar shows: the test platform's `set_menus` ignores the keymap. The unit tests pin what `key_table(true)` hands the menu code, and a probe that is not committed applied the platform's own rule to the real keymap; see the notes.

Other menu bar items, from that probe. Left because order can't fix them: each has one key or none, so showing Finder's would mean binding a new key. Finder's keys here are from memory, not checked. File › Rename… shows F2 (Finder shows no key). File › Explore Data shows Cmd+Space (Spotlight's default; the manual already says so). View › Toggle Sidebar shows Alt+Cmd+S (I believe current Finder shows Ctrl+Cmd+S). Make Alias, Put Back and Use Groups have no key (Finder: Ctrl+Cmd+A, Cmd+Backspace, Ctrl+Cmd+0), nor has Go › Trash. Window › Copy to Other Pane (F5), Move to Other Pane (F6) and fffinder's own commands have one key each and no Finder counterpart. Everything else with more than one key has the Mac's first: Back, Forward, Enclosing Folder, Move to Trash, and Show Next/Previous Tab (Ctrl+Tab, as in Finder's Window menu). Edit › Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy and Paste get Cmd+Z and the rest from the kit's own macOS bindings, which are bound before fffinder's (read in gpui-base, not run).
F6 and F2 outside the file views on a Mac are untouched: if macOS offers them to the menu bar they reach Window › Move to Other Pane and File › Rename…, as before.
Linux and Windows menus deliberately keep Enter for Open, Ctrl+Y for Quick Look and Ctrl+R for Refresh, and F5 stays a key of the file views there; see Found, not fixed.
The manual's menu bar table gives keys for some items only and wasn't made wrong, so Open, Quick Look and Refresh got none there.
No assertion that Refresh runs once with its keys bound twice: a second refresh can't be observed. Open and Quick Look are asserted.
`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: src/term is untouched and no signature changed.
CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.

Fails without the change: left ["f5", "ctrl-r"], right ["ctrl-r", "f5", "f5", "ctrl-r"] for finder::Refresh)

review_fixes: Bound F5 -> Refresh in the FINDER context on a Mac, in the first `if mac` block after Cmd+R, so Cmd+R stays the first key bound and the one the menu bar shows. The implementer reported, and left, that with Cmd+R on View › Refresh the only menu bar item with F5 is Window › Copy to Other Pane, so an F5 the window doesn't take (pressed in the search field, the sidebar, the tree, or a name being edited) would go from refreshing to a warning in a window with one pane and to a copy in split view. The brief asks that no key change what it does. Bound in the window, F5 refreshes there whatever the menu bar would do, and in the file views the table's F5 bindings are deeper and still win. Checked with the Mac's table bound on Linux: F5 in the search field refreshed, in split view too, where nothing was copied and no warning showed; F5 in a split view's files still copied; the background menu still showed Ctrl+R for Refresh, not F5. To undo it: remove the `key("f5", Refresh, &finder, cx)` line and the second paragraph of the comment above the block, the second "f5" in CMD_KEY_ACTIONS, the two FINDER assertions in the unit tests, and tests/basics.rs f5_refreshes_outside_the_file_views_on_a_mac.

Unit tests: the Mac's list of Refresh's keys gained the F5, and both tests now pin which context has it (FINDER on a Mac, none off one). Renamed ..._have_no_key_bound_again_off_a_mac to ..._have_only_the_tables_keys_off_a_mac: its expected lists hold Return and Space twice, for two contexts, so the old name read wrong.
Added tests/basics.rs f5_refreshes_outside_the_file_views_on_a_mac, beside the other F5 tests.

Commit message: the paragraph that reported the F5 change as a side effect now describes the binding and says which part is taken on trust; what the runs with the Mac's table showed; and that the menu items stay unavailable while a dialog has the keyboard.

Rebased twice: 7228253 and then e746db6 landed during the review. No conflicts. check.sh printed CHECK OK before the rebases and after each (567, 579 and 584 tests passed as the trunk grew), and the suite with the Mac's table forced was run again on 7228253.
notes:
CHECK ONCE ON A MAC (nothing here could run there): View › Refresh shows Cmd+R, File › Open shows Cmd+O and File › Quick Look shows Cmd+Y; the item menu (right-click a file) shows Cmd+O beside Open; one press of Cmd+O opens once, and Cmd+Y opens Quick Look and a second press closes it; F5 with the keyboard in the search field refreshes and, in split view, copies nothing; Cmd+O and Cmd+Y pressed in the search field open and show the selection (expected, by reading; see behaviour_changes). macOS CI runs two tests with Mac-only expectations: tests/controls.rs menus_in_the_window_show_this_systems_keys_for_open_quick_look_and_refresh (kbd:cmd-o, kbd:cmd-y and kbd:cmd-r drawn; kbd:enter, kbd:space and kbd:f5 not) and tests/basics.rs f5_refreshes_outside_the_file_views_on_a_mac. If the reading of the kit is wrong, CI fails there.

What I verified, and how. (1) Read gpui-pre-macos 0.3.10 src/platform.rs `create_menu_item` and gpui-pre 0.3.10 src/keymap.rs: the menu bar's key is the action's first binding unless one has no context or matches Zed's Workspace/Pane/Editor context; `set_menus` runs after `bind_keys` (src/lib.rs `init`). (2) A probe test, not committed, applied that rule to the real keymap, kit bindings included, with the Mac's table bound on Linux: Open ctrl-o, Quick Look ctrl-y, Refresh ctrl-r, Copy to Other Pane f5, and no two different commands share a key (Redo's ctrl-y in that run is the kit's Linux binding; on macOS the kit binds Cmd+Shift+Z). (3) With `key_table(true, cx)` forced in `bind_keys` (not committed) the whole suite failed only the three root-only tests and the two per-system tests of 918c6a7 (the_item_menu_shows_this_systems_keys_for_move_to_trash and the_keys_shown_for_going_back_forward_and_up_are_this_systems, whose Linux expectations a Mac's table can't meet); the new controls test passed with its macOS expectations spelled with Ctrl, and the new basics test with its early return taken out. (4) `Window::is_action_available` for Open, Quick Look, Refresh and Copy to Other Pane is false while the Go to Folder, Settings, Search Syntax and New File dialogs have the keyboard, and true in the search field and while a name is edited in place. (5) gpui-pre-macos src/window.rs `handle_key_event` answers NO for a key equivalent that no binding handled, which is when AppKit asks the menu bar, and the kit's text field swallows no key it has no binding for. (6) Dispatched from the search field as the menu bar would, Open opened the selected file once and Quick Look opened once.

What I could not verify: anything AppKit does. In particular that a plain F5 is offered to the menu bar (function keys carry the Function flag, and GPUI's own code handles key equivalents that have only that flag, which is why I believe it), and that of two enabled items with the same key equivalent the first one wins. The F5 binding makes both beside the point for F5. Plain Return and Space are not offered to the menu bar ahead of the window: if they were, a space typed in the search field would have opened Quick Look on every Mac until now.

For briefs still to come:
- Any brief that adds, removes or moves a key of Refresh, Open or Quick Look, in any context (type-select-space, preview-page-keys, quick-look-empty-state, split-active-pane, show-in-enclosing-folder-key): `CMD_KEY_ACTIONS` in the tests of src/actions.rs pins every key of those three in bound order, on a Mac and off one; update it. Keep the Mac's Cmd key the first one bound (the first `if mac` block) and, for Open, the last (the block at the end). `open_selected`, `quick_look` and `refresh` must not call `cx.propagate()` after acting: on a Mac Cmd+O is bound three times and Cmd+Y and Cmd+R twice. tests/finder.rs open_quick_look_and_refresh_act_once_with_their_keys_bound_twice presses them that way.
- type-select-space: the Space -> QuickLook line is where it was. A new `TypeSpace` action bound to Space after it leaves QuickLook's own bindings, which are what CMD_KEY_ACTIONS pins, alone. Its handler passing the key on when it did nothing is fine; `quick_look` itself must go on not passing it on. On a Mac File › Quick Look's key equivalent is now Cmd+Y, so the menu bar has no claim on Space.
- split-active-pane: (a) its plan says "bind shift-tab first and tab last, so the menu bar shows Tab". That is the wrong way round: the macOS menu bar shows the FIRST key bound, and the window's own menus and tooltips the last. Bind Tab first for the menu bar. (b) On a Mac F5 is bound to Refresh in the FINDER context (first block of `key_table`); the file views' F5 bindings win there because their context is deeper. If Copy to Other Pane is to work from more of a pane than its file views, narrow or drop that binding, and change the FINDER assertions in the unit tests and tests/basics.rs f5_refreshes_outside_the_file_views_on_a_mac with it. (c) Copy to Other Pane and Move to Other Pane in the item menu will show F5 and F6: each has one key.
- show-in-enclosing-folder-key: a `secondary-enter` binding inside the table leaves Open's first and last key on a Mac alone. The new controls test looks for `kbd:enter` in the item menu off a Mac and for its absence on one; `kbd:ctrl-enter` and `kbd:cmd-enter` are different selectors, so a hint beside the new item doesn't trip it. Its note that the menu bar dispatches from the search field holds for Cmd+O and Cmd+Y too now.
- context-menus-fit: tests/controls.rs menus_in_the_window_show_this_systems_keys_for_open_quick_look_and_refresh right-clicks a file row and then empty space in the list view of an ordinary folder and looks for the key hints beside Open, Quick Look and Refresh. Keep those items and their actions there, or change the test with them.
- What the item menu shows for Open off a Mac (Enter) depends on the folder tree's Return -> OpenSelected being bound after the files' Cmd+O. That test pins it.

Found, not fixed:
- The manual says F5 refreshes in the window ("Cmd+R | Refresh (F5 too, outside split view)" under "In the window", and "Refresh (Cmd+R; F5 outside split view)"), but on Linux and Windows F5 is bound in the file views only: with the keyboard in the search field, the sidebar or the tree it does nothing. A Mac refreshes there. Binding F5 -> Refresh in the FINDER context on every system would make the manual true; this brief leaves Linux and Windows alone.
- On a Mac, F6 outside the file views reaches Window › Move to Other Pane through the menu bar, if macOS offers function keys to it: a move in split view, a warning otherwise. F2 and File › Rename… are the same case. Both were so before.
- While a name is being edited in place the menu bar's items stay available, because the edit is inside the browser. So on a Mac Cmd+O and Cmd+Y now open or show the file being renamed and leave the edit open, as choosing File › Open with the mouse always could.
- File › Explore Data shows Cmd+Space, which is Spotlight's default on a Mac (the manual already says so).
